segments.source: Discussion
segments.ko: Discussion

segments.source: Create a matrix using data from a buffer of floats.
segments.ko: Create a matrix using data from a buffer of floats.

segments.source: Ownership of the buffer is transferred from the caller to the returned object.
segments.ko: Ownership of the buffer is transferred from the caller to the returned object.

segments.source: This function creates an object representing a matrix whose entries are copied out of the supplied buffer of floats.
segments.ko: This function creates an object representing a matrix whose entries are copied out of the supplied buffer of floats.

segments.source: Negative or zero strides are not supported by this function (but note that you can reverse the rows or columns using the la_matrix_slice function defined below).
segments.ko: Negative or zero strides are not supported by this function (but note that you can reverse the rows or columns using the la_matrix_slice function defined below).

segments.source: This routine assumes that the elements of the matrix are stored in the buffer in row-major order.
segments.ko: This routine assumes that the elements of the matrix are stored in the buffer in row-major order.

segments.source: If you need to work with data that is in column-major order, you can do that as follows:
segments.ko: If you need to work with data that is in column-major order, you can do that as follows:

segments.source: Use this routine to create a matrix object, but pass the number of columns in your matrix for the matrix_rows parameter and vice-versa.  For the matrix_row_stride parameter, pass the column stride of your matrix.
segments.ko: Use this routine to create a matrix object, but pass the number of columns in your matrix for the matrix_rows parameter and vice-versa.  For the matrix_row_stride parameter, pass the column stride of your matrix.

segments.source: Make a new matrix transpose object from the object created in step 1.  The resulting object represents the matrix that you want to work with.
segments.ko: Make a new matrix transpose object from the object created in step 1.  The resulting object represents the matrix that you want to work with.

segments.source: Parameters
segments.ko: Parameters

segments.source: `buffer`: Pointer to float data providing the elements of the matrix.
segments.ko: `buffer`: Pointer to float data providing the elements of the matrix.

segments.source: `matrix_rows`: The number of rows in the matrix.
segments.ko: `matrix_rows`: The number of rows in the matrix.

segments.source: `matrix_cols`: The number of columns in the matrix.
segments.ko: `matrix_cols`: The number of columns in the matrix.

segments.source: `matrix_row_stride`: The offset in the buffer (measured in floats) between corresponding elements in consecutive rows of the matrix.  Must be positive.
segments.ko: `matrix_row_stride`: The offset in the buffer (measured in floats) between corresponding elements in consecutive rows of the matrix.  Must be positive.

segments.source: `matrix_hint`: Flags describing special matrix structures.
segments.ko: `matrix_hint`: Flags describing special matrix structures.

segments.source: `deallocator`: Callback to be used to deallocate the buffer when the returned matrix object is destroyed.
segments.ko: `deallocator`: Callback to be used to deallocate the buffer when the returned matrix object is destroyed.

segments.source: `attributes`: Attributes to attach to the new la_object_t object.  Pass LA_DEFAULT_ATTRIBUTES to create a normal object.
segments.ko: `attributes`: Attributes to attach to the new la_object_t object.  Pass LA_DEFAULT_ATTRIBUTES to create a normal object.
